text.p: Italian debt markets swept higher on continued EMU convergence trading, with the front month Btp future on LIFFE carving out yet another record high.
The spread of the 10-year cash Btp over the 10-year Bund cranked in another few notches to 80 basis points, also a record, as BTP buying from all directions kept up momentum.

Dealers said both the future and the spread could clock up more records in coming weeks, with Europe looking set to head for a single European currency and Italy seen as likely to join in the first wave.

Dealers said the lightning progress of the Btp market was breathtaking. "If you'd stood up two years ago in any dealing room and said the big trade that's going to make your bank lots of money is Italy-Germany, you'd have been locked up and the key thrown away," said Jonathan York at Mees Pierson in London.
The September futures contract on LIFFE was 58 basis points stronger at 138.14 after peaking at a record 138.44 earlier.
"I'd like to see a bit of consolidation but with the way the market is trading there hasn't been much consolidation," York said. "The peak is 138.44 and there's no reason not to break that tomorrow."
The February 2007 Btp ended 50 basis points higher at 103.62 while the lira proved rather more steady, sitting close to Tuesday's levels of 972.00 per mark.
In Italy, traders noted the market remained positive but showed a little caution after late profit-taking.
